ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Identify the number of species with no natural predator on this food web.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is titled "Chesapeake Bay Waterbird Food Web". The food web lists Primary Producers, Herbivores, Primary Consumers, Secondary Consumers, Tertiary Consumers, etc. by levels, includes labels such as Phytoplankton, Zooplankton, Small Planktivorous Fish, Large Piscivorous Fish, Osprey, Bald Eagle, Gulls and Terns, Wading Birds, Sea Ducks, Tundra Swan, Herbivorous Ducks, Geese and Mute Swans, etc., and connects them with arrows. Reasoning: First determine the direction of the arrows. In the figure, the arrows from Phytoplankton and Zooplankton point to Small Planktivorous Fish, and the arrow from Large Piscivorous Fish points to Osprey and Bald Eagle, so the arrows indicate from food/prey to consumer/predator. To find species with "no natural predators" is to find terminal species with no arrows continuing from them to other species. After scanning the visible labels one by one, the terminal species are Osprey, Bald Eagle, Gulls and Terns, Wading Birds, Tundra Swan, Herbivorous Ducks, Geese and Mute Swans, a total of 7.
